worker_runtime_basis.what: per seed run, a separate probe process started with the worker's PATH and command interpreter records the interpreter, prefix, library versions and package-list hash; every record must equal the approved venv (validate_worker_records)
worker_runtime_basis.limitation: the probe does not attest the task process itself ([AS]: NOT CHECKABLE); accepted and disclosed under R1-B2-GO B4 (a)

environment_basis.disclosure: R1-B2-GO B6 (a): no environment freeze bound to the sweep-1 launch exists. The B.2 audit environment is established by the published, independently reviewed e1 environment replay (docs/r1/reports/e1_replay_20261117/REPORT.md, sha256 5892913533416e5e8c66ae913a46528a29be69e483eaecd2ca04929b5dad0048, at 52992b22; review E1_AMEND_RUN_REVIEW_20261117.md ACCEPTED; 16/16 cases at tolerance 0) and by re-running that replay's current-environment checks (r1/scripts/c3_env_replay.py check_environment: wrapper target, Python and library versions, uv.lock, the 25 Oct freeze plus narwhals, dist-info mtimes) at audit start; the current package list, interpreter build, prefix, wrapper target and newest dist-info mtime must equal the replay's recorded values. This is a current-state observation, not a launch-bound snapshot. Carried from the replay report (section 9): (1) dataset identity for the six OpenML nodes rests on the amended evidence of R1-E1-OPENML-AMEND (sweep-1 data id, sweep-1 loaded-data fingerprint recomputed equal, OpenML md5 self-consistency, and audited cache bytes unchanged since the 16 Nov audit), not on a file hash recorded by sweep 1; the surviving cache bytes are not anchored by a hash the sweep-1 launch wrote; (2) the batch .venv executables are wrappers to the shared venv /ceph/dwong/r1_prepare_20261025/venv, not a separately built venv; (3) the replay is a bounded reproducibility check of 16 worker evaluations, reconstructed from uv.lock and the batch venv; it is not proof that every original dependency or all 288 roots were identical, and it says nothing about LLM seed replay. The batch harness is tracked-clean; its only untracked files are the six OpenML data caches (tree digests required equal to the e1 post-run record) and paper/tables/artifact_completeness_report.txt, as the e1 record states.
